subject.title: [Feature]: Inbound media shared across all agents — no per-agent isolation

question: What durable identity and compatibility contract should OpenClaw use for inbound-media isolation across storage, managed references, staging, cleanup, and channel/plugin APIs?
rationale: The source evidence proves the flat media pool remains, but choosing account, resolved agent, session, channel/chat, tenant, or indexed provenance is a security and compatibility decision automation should not invent.

options.title: Adopt a scoped managed-media contract
options.body: Define the core scoped media contract and update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

options.title: Start with account or channel subdirs
options.body: Use sanitized channel/account identifiers as the first isolation step while accepting that session/chat/tenant provenance remains follow-up work.

options.title: Defer to media-index design
options.body: Keep this tracker open until maintainers choose a media-index or provenance schema instead of changing filesystem layout first.

recommendation.title: Adopt a scoped managed-media contract
recommendation.body: Define the core scoped media contract and update bundled channels, resolvers, staging, cleanup, docs, and tests together.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest routing signal is the prior review plus repeated core media-reference and sandbox-staging history.
